# Lighthouse Prep

> SAT preparation and college guidance for students applying to selective colleges. Online and one-on-one, anywhere in the US. The two coaches, Allan and Jon, teach every session, and every program price is published.

Every family works with both coaches on one shared plan, and parents can see progress every week. Every session runs on video, so we work with families anywhere in the US and schedule around your time zone. Sessions are recorded only if a parent gives consent. Our services are for students 13 and older, with a parent's consent.

We don't guarantee admission or a specific result. Every program includes the +100 point promise, with its terms below.

## Programs and prices

- SAT Accelerator: $4,400. 20 coaching hours, one-on-one, online. SAT preparation with Allan. For students whose main need is a stronger SAT score.
- Flagship Program (recommended): $7,600. 40 coaching hours. SAT preparation with Allan; essay review, interview preparation and career guidance with Jon; 1 recorded mock interview with written feedback. For juniors and rising seniors applying to selective colleges.
- Premier Program: $9,200. 50 coaching hours. SAT preparation with Allan; essay review, interview preparation and career guidance with Jon; 3 recorded mock interviews with written feedback; an introduction to an industry professional in a field your student is exploring. For families who want the most time with both coaches.
- All three include the parent and student dashboard (weekly plans and progress) and the +100 point promise: if your student completes the full plan and improves by fewer than 100 points from the diagnostic to an official SAT, we add 8 hours of tutoring at no cost.
- Payment: pay in full and save 5% ($4,180, $7,220 or $8,740), or split any program into three monthly payments ($1,466.66, $2,533.33 or $3,066.66 a month for three months, then nothing more).

## Enrolling

- You can enroll directly from the programs on the [home page](https://thelighthouseprep.com/#programs): each program has an Enroll button. Choose to pay in full and save 5%, or three monthly payments: the first today, then the same day of the next two months.
- Payment runs through Stripe's secure checkout, so we never see your card number. Your portal invitation arrives by email within minutes of paying; a bank payment takes up to four business days to clear first.
- After paying: set your password from the invitation, tell us about your student on the portal's first screen (two minutes), and we get in touch within one business day to schedule the diagnostic and the first session.
- [Enrollment terms](https://thelighthouseprep.com/terms/): what you're buying, paying, changing your mind (tell us after the first two sessions, before the third, and we refund everything you've paid beyond those two sessions), recordings and your student's account.
- Prefer to talk first? Book a free consult (below).

## Who teaches

- Allan, SAT tutor: Allan has taught the SAT and ACT for 10+ years and spent 6 years in the classroom. His students gain an average of 350 points from their first practice test to their official score, and he has coached 200+ students.
- Jon, college counselor: Jon works with families on college lists, essays in the student's own words, and interviews. He holds a Wharton MBA, is an ex-McKinsey consultant and a veteran US Navy officer, and has 8+ years in high-impact leadership roles. He is a former admissions vice president at Penn and a Certified Professional Mentor (CPM).

## The free consult

- [Book a free 20-minute consult](https://thelighthouseprep.com/#consult): tell us a little about your student and we will reply within one business day to find a time. A short call about your student's goals and timeline, a free review of a recent PSAT, SAT or practice test, and a written plan within 24 hours of the review.
- Email: hello@thelighthouseprep.com

## Guides

- [What your PSAT score means, and what to do next](https://thelighthouseprep.com/guides/what-your-psat-score-means/): PSAT scores arrive Oct 22, Nov 5 or Nov 12. How to read the report, what a good score is for your student, National Merit, and what to do next. By Allan and Jon; last reviewed October 6, 2026.
